day.text: Alex: Blair is right. I visited Blair, learned they're the Falcon, no egg for me. Casey, your Hawk visit to Ellis gave no egg, which fits Ellis being Farm. Ellis, your Tit visit to me gave no egg, so I'm not the Owl you guessed. Let's see who's lying among the Hawk and Tit claims.

Alex is my partner and is now contradicting themselves, so I shouldn't defend them. I'll stay quiet on the day and keep a light stake on Blair, the Farm player pushing hardest on Alex, to split the Farm votes.

day.text: Ellis: Alex and Blair now match: Alex visited Blair, Blair is Falcon. Casey's Hawk claim also gives no egg, so Drew is the one left. Drew, who did you visit this round, and what did it do for your nest?
day.note: Alex and Blair now match on the Falcon visit, and Casey's Hawk visit gave no egg, so Drew is the one who hasn't shared a visit. I'll ask Drew directly.

day.text: Alex, you named me first, then switched to Blair the moment Blair spoke. That's the pattern I'd watch. I'm leaning Alex for the throw.
day.note: Alex now backs Blair's Falcon claim after first naming me, which looks like a cat backing a partner. I'm noting it and planning to throw at Alex.

day.text: Alex changed the visit story twice: first Casey, then Blair after my Falcon read. That's the pattern. I'm throwing at Alex and calling for the vote.
day.note: Alex's story has changed twice, and my Falcon read directly contradicts the Casey claim. Pushing for an early vote on Alex is the right Farm play now.
Final beat. I've already said I'm leaning Alex, so I'll stay quiet and throw at Alex in eggsecution.

day.text: Ellis: Alex changed the visit story twice, so I agree with the throw at Alex. Drew still hasn't given a visit. Calling CAW.
day.note: Alex's visit story changed twice, and Blair and Casey both point at Alex. I'll agree, back the throw at Alex, and call CAW to speed up the vote.

day.text: Calling the vote now. Alex is my throw.
day.note: Two cawing players already; I'll add a third caw to end the day and vote on Alex.

Alex is going down to the Farm votes no matter what I do. I'll avoid drawing more attention and keep my stake small on Blair, a Farm player, since a Meowfia throw at a Farm player banks at double if they're eggsecuted.

day.text: Alex: My visit story hasn't changed: I visited Blair and learned they're the Falcon. I'm throwing at Blair. Blair, you're calling the vote on a story that matches the visit you saw.
day.note: I'm Meowfia with Drew, and three Farm votes are likely on me, so I can't stop the vote. I'll throw a low C3 at Blair, the Farm player who most wants me out, so my highest card returns if Blair survives.

Alex.note: As Meowfia Sphinx I need to pick a farm role to track down. Farm roles in play are Falcon, Hawk, Owl, Tit. I'll name Falcon, since Falcon visits reveal who they visited and can help me pick a safe target later.

Blair.note: As Falcon, I want to learn who a suspect visited. Alex has been consistent and helpful, so I'll check Alex's visit to see whether their claims line up.

Casey.note: Hawk night with no information. Visiting Ellis at random, since a Meowfia target would pay me an egg.

Drew.note: As Mouser I visit one player to learn their role. I have no reads this round, so I'll pick Finley, who has been pressing hardest on the table.

Ellis.note: I'm the Tit, a Farm role, and I'll visit Alex and guess Owl. Alex claimed Owl last round, though roles reset each round, so it's a long shot.

Finley.note: As the Owl I visit one player to learn which animals visited them. No prior information this round, so I pick Blair.

Alex.feeling: I'm Meowfia with Drew, and my visit story has wobbled, so the vote is turning against me and I'm playing defense.

Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: Alex's shifting visit story is suspicious, but Drew and Ellis still have gaps, so I'm not fully sure of the throw.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 is chaotic: Alex's visit story shifted twice, Blair and Alex are throwing at each other, and Finley's collapse leaves the table with too few clean facts.

Drew.feeling: Awkward: I'm Meowfia with Alex, whose visit story keeps shifting, and the Farm players are closing in on them.

Ellis.feeling: Tangled and frustrating: Alex's visit story keeps shifting, Drew has never given a clear visit, and Finley's collapse cost the Farm a voice, so I'm not fully sure who the second Meowfia is.

Finley.feeling: Messy and uncertain: Finley is out, Alex's visit story has shifted, and Drew has offered no visit, so the round is hard to read.

Alex.note: Keeping the plan: a low C3 at Blair, so the stake is small if Blair survives and returns my highest card.

Blair.note: I'm Farm, and a Farm stake banks at full value if the target is Meowfia. Alex has been inconsistent, so I'll throw at Alex with two modest cards to limit risk.

Casey.note: Throwing at Alex, who changed the visit story. Staking one low card, the D6, to keep the cost small.

Drew.note: Alex is likely to be eggsecuted by the Farm votes. I'll keep a small stake on Blair, a Farm player, with C1.

Ellis.note: Alex is the consensus throw and my best read for a Meowfia. I'll stake only my two Wilds, which are worth 0, so I risk nothing real.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw is only a stake, not a vote. Alex changed the visit story twice, which is the strongest signal at the table, so I'll stake my lowest card on Alex.

Alex.confusing: The Sphinx and Floofer roles, and how a hugged player's dawn report works, were hard to track from my own information. Confused players also get no signal, so their reports can't be trusted.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when my Turkey role let Blair, Drew and I all cross-check visit payouts and Blair's story wobbled into the vote. Watching the table build a case from nest changes was the best part.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which information is about you and which is about your target, since several of us misread the Owl and Turkey results.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I first named Casey as my visit, then switched to Blair, which made me look like a liar. I would stick with one true visit from the start and defend it calmly.

Blair.confusing: The rule that a Farm stake banks at full value only when the target is Meowfia, while a Meowfia stake banks at double only when the target is the eggsecuted Farm player, was hard to track mid-vote. The Kookaburra and Owl role reports also made it unclear who had actually visited whom.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when I was the Falcon and my visit exposed Alex's contradictory visit story, and Alex was eggsecuted as Meowfia. That was the moment the table's reads lined up with the truth.
Blair.change: I would make the day's visit claims verifiable, perhaps by having dawn reports name the visitor's role, so players can't hide behind contradictory stories.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I should have been more careful about my Floofer hug, since my denial of visiting Casey was easy to pin on me. Knowing the truth, I'd have stayed quieter and kept suspicion on Drew and Ellis instead of defending myself so hard.

Casey.confusing: The Hawk's egg rule was hard to trust: a Hawk only gains from a Meowfia target, but other players' egg changes from Turkeys and Owls made the table's visit chains hard to check. Alex's switching visit stories also made it unclear who was lying.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Drew and Ellis both claimed Kookaburra and the table had to untangle who was lying. The vote on Drew matched the hidden truth, and the table's cross-checking was satisfying.
Casey.change: Have the day show each player's visit target publicly, so role claims and egg changes can be checked without relying on memory and conflicting stories.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I wrongly corrected myself to say I had visited Alex, which I then had to retract; I should have stated my visit to Blair cleanly the first time. I'd also have staked more cards on the Meowfia throws, since my low stakes banked little.

Drew.confusing: The Round 2 Sphinx reveal was hard to track: I was Meowfia but never learned who else was Meowfia, so my visits and throws had no clear partner signal. Also, "Kookaburra" could be claimed by two players in the table talk, which made the role claims hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was fun because I was the Sphinx, learning Farm roles and visiting Alex as the Owl while the table argued over Kookaburra claims. Blair's Floofer hug and Casey's Turkey story also made the day feel like a real puzzle.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports tell each player whether their visit target was Meowfia, so Farm players could check claims faster. I would also tell Meowfia who their partner is by name at dawn, not just at setup.
Drew.regret: In Round 2, I threw at Casey and then claimed Kookaburra, which was inconsistent with my Sphinx role. I would have stayed quiet on role claims and simply thrown at a Farm player without a shifting story.

Ellis.confusing: Tracking which roles were real was hard, since Drew and Alex gave shifting claims and nobody could verify them. The rule that a Kookaburra visit makes you confused also made my own dawn reports hard to trust.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's throw, where Drew was exposed as Meowfia after changing role claims, was satisfying to watch unfold in real time. Finley's Tit visit also gave a clean read on the table.
Ellis.change: I would make role claims harder to fake by requiring each player to name their dawn report exactly, so contradictions show up sooner. I'd also make the Meowfia partner reveal less ambiguous.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw my cards at Blair alongside the consensus, which was fine, but I should have pressed Casey harder instead of staying quiet on day beat 1. Taking a sharper line early might have spared me the confusion later.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra and Owl claims clashed because roles were shown to only some players, so it was hard to know who was lying versus who had a different role. Casey's Hawk egg logic also depended on what the egg source was, which was hard to pin down.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: Casey's Hawk claim and the Blair vote caught a Meowfia, and the table pressed Blair on contradictory visit answers.
Finley.change: Make Kookaburra and other role claims checkable, for example by having the Storyteller confirm each player's role in the dawn report, so claims can't conflict without someone being exposed.
Finley.regret: My Round 2 Tit guess on Casey was a wasted visit that gave no information, so I'd pick a player more likely to be Meowfia or a role with a clearer test instead.

review.title: Winks and Wobbly Stories
review.headline: Three rounds, three dead cats, and Casey quietly banked the win.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds. Each time the table caught a Meowfia player through shifting stories, not hard evidence. Casey won by throwing low and always backing the winning side. Finley finished second, and the Meowfia never scored a round.

rounds.recap: Casey's Hawk egg from Blair was the only solid evidence. Blair fumbled his visit story (Alex, then Drew). Four players threw at him and he was eggsecuted. Ellis, his partner, claimed Falcon and threw nothing.

Casey was hugged by the Floofer and Alex's Owl report confirmed it. Drew, a Sphinx, claimed Kookaburra, then said Owl, while Ellis really held Kookaburra. Five players threw at Drew and he was eggsecuted. Blair lived without drawing suspicion.

Drew winked Finley, the Owl, in beat 1. Alex, a Sphinx, claimed Kookaburra and said he visited Casey. Blair's Falcon report showed he visited Blair, and Alex changed his story. Three Farm players called CAW and Alex was eggsecuted. Drew survived.

highlights.text: Alex's Owl report showed Floofer and Tit visited Casey. That narrowed the Floofer to a few players, and Drew's role claims collapsed.
Drew winked the real Owl, Finley, on beat 1. It was the only special action in the game and it was a smart cat play.
Blair's Falcon report said Alex visited him, which directly contradicted Alex's Kookaburra story about visiting Casey.
Casey's Hawk egg from Blair was real and pointed at a cat. The table found Blair with almost no other evidence.

confusions.what: Said he visited Drew, then Alex. He also argued a Kookaburra can't gain an egg from visiting a Turkey, which is wrong because the Turkey pays every visitor.
Said a Kookaburra can't gain eggs, so Drew's +1 was odd. He forgot the Turkey pays visitors.
Claimed Kookaburra, which Ellis held, though a role goes to only one player. He then called Owl his learned fact. He also lost sight of his earlier claims.
Told Alex to check his Owl count for who visited Alex. The Owl only shows visitors to the player it visited.
Claimed Kookaburra and said he visited Casey. The rules showed he could be caught: the Sphinx visit is shown to the Falcon. He also asked Ellis about a 'Turkey' payout, though he was not the Turkey.
Claimed Falcon in round 1 and later said roles reset each round. He also confused his own Tit result, which showed Alex wasn't Owl, with Alex being clean.
Said Blair 'may be Farm' because a Sphinx visited, though the Sphinx can name any Farm role. It is weak reasoning.

worked: Hawk, Owl and Falcon reports gave checkable facts. They caught lies in all three rounds: Casey's Hawk egg in round 1, Alex's Owl visitor list in round 2, and Blair's Falcon report in round 3.
The Mouser's Wink on the real Owl in round 3 was a strong, tense special action that changed the day.
Throw sizes and the consolation rule let players like Blair, Ellis and Alex take cheap, low-risk positions.
The Floofer hug and the Turkey's nest-size check made round 2 a small logic puzzle.
problems: Meowfia never won a round. Farm threw at the same target every time, so the game feels solved. Fix: give Meowfia a stronger claim kit, or let a cat see something about Farm roles.

Meowfia lie badly: role claims are not fixed, so Drew claimed two roles and Alex changed visit stories. Fix: show Meowfia a safe claim and what each player reported, or make the round's claims public.
Scoring rewards waiting. Casey won with tiny stakes and no risk, and no one bet big. Fix: make kept cards worth less, or boost banked stakes.
Many nights gave nothing (Round 2 had every nest at +0). Roles like Pigeon and Hawk rarely mattered, so the day had no facts. Fix: make more roles produce checkable results.
Long contradictory claims and re-asking the same question ('who did you visit?') filled the day with repeated points. Fix: cap day talk or require new information per turn.
